results.evidence: Section 9.3(c): Buyer shall indemnify the Seller Parties against "all Losses under any Seller Credit Support, including any payment, reimbursement, draw or other amount paid or payable by any Seller Party under or in respect of such Seller Credit Support." Section 9.5(d): "The Indemnity Cap, the Deductible and the survival periods in Section 9.1 apply only to claims under Sections 9.2(a) and 9.3(a)."

The aggregate amount of Losses that the Buyer Indemnitees may recover, whether by set-off under this Article 6, by withholding under Section 6.2(b), by direct payment from Holder or otherwise, shall, notwithstanding Section 9.5(b) of the Purchase Agreement, not exceed the Indemnity Cap, other than Losses arising from Fraud.

Recital C: "Under Section 2.4(a) of the Purchase Agreement, Holder delivered the Closing Statement on June 12, 2026. No Dispute Notice was delivered before the end of the Review Period, and the Closing Statement became final and binding on the parties under Section 2.4(b) of the Purchase Agreement."

SPA §9.1(b): "The Fundamental Representations, the representations and warranties in Section 4.12 (Taxes), and Seller's obligations under Section 9.2(c) shall survive the Closing until the Note Maturity Date." Article I: "'Note Maturity Date' means the maturity date of the Seller Note, as amended from time to time." A&R Seller Note §2.1: "The entire unpaid principal balance of this Note ... is due and payable on December 31, 2026 (the 'Maturity Date')."

Section 9.1 says: "This Note, and any dispute concerning payment, set-off or recovery under this Note or under Article IX of the Purchase Agreement as applied to this Note, shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York." Section 9.2 adds: "Each of Maker and Holder irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state courts of the State of New York sitting in New York County and the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York for any action or proceeding arising out of this Note, including any dispute concerning payment, set-off or recovery."
